title: Urbanisation is a rising share

blocks.heading: Urbanisation is a rising share
blocks.text: Urbanisation is an increase in the proportion of a population living in urban areas; distinguish it from an increase in urban population alone. Urban share is urban population divided by total population, multiplied by 100; a larger urban number does not prove a larger share. Use consistent urban definitions and a stated area and period. In a fictional country, 400,000 of 1,000,000 people are urban: 40%. Later, 600,000 of 2,000,000 are urban: 30%. The urban number rises by 200,000, yet its share falls by 10 percentage points. These figures therefore do not show urbanisation over that interval. A percentage-point change compares the shares directly; it is different from percentage growth in the urban count.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Calculate the share before naming the trend
blocks.text: For a separate fictional calculation, 360,000 urban residents among 900,000 total gives 360,000 ÷ 900,000 = 0.4. Multiplying by 100 gives 40%. For a trend, compare at least two periods: if the next comparable share is 45%, the increase is five percentage points. Topic 7.1 explains population measures. Urbanisation concerns the changing urban share, urban growth the urban number; check which the prompt asks for.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect causes and responses
blocks.text: Use the denominator and a comparable definition before describing urbanisation. Population in Topic 7.1 supplies related measures.
